products.name: Ollama
products.note: Local LLM runner; self-hosted; no data exfiltration; model supply-chain verification needed

reading.body:
Ollama, founded in 2023, lets users run open-source language models locally on their own hardware, keeping all data private and offline by default.

The company positions local execution as the core offering, with cloud capacity as an optional add-on for higher throughput. This inverts the typical SaaS model where cloud is primary and local is secondary. The architecture matters for AI infrastructure because it moves compute from centralized data centers to distributed user machines, which means no single building or power connection is a binding constraint on how many people can run models. It also means Ollama itself does not directly consume grid power for inference the way cloud providers do.

The data does not cover how many users Ollama has, what models run on it, or how much compute actually moved to local execution versus remaining in Ollama's cloud. It also does not address the supply-chain risks the profile text flags, or whether model weights hosted on the platform have been verified for source and integrity. The economics of local versus cloud inference for different workloads remain outside this record.

profile_text.body:
Ollama is a company founded in 2023. Its website describes the product as the easiest way to automate work using open models while keeping data safe. The site states that cloud models are hosted in the US, Europe, and Singapore, that data is never trained on by any provider, and that local models are always free. It also describes dedicated capacity for running several agents at once and pricing that starts free with usage upgrades.

The product is listed as Ollama, an open-source and self-hosted local LLM runner. Its note states no data exfiltration and flags that model supply-chain verification is needed.
